The research series · Case files 001 to 011

Seeing at
a Distance

Remote viewing is a 1970s laboratory program. Astral projection is a 19th century name for a much older claim. This page holds the documented record for both, the ancient material that resembles them, and the honest places where the record stops.

Labels used throughout: DOCUMENTED (primary records) · REPORTED (first-person testimony) · LEGEND (a culture's story) · DISPUTED (the same record, different verdicts).

The modern record · File 011

A Real Program, Honestly Bounded

Remote viewing research began at SRI International in 1972, with physicists Russell Targ and Harold Puthoff. The artist Ingo Swann had suggested the name "remote viewing" a year earlier, in December 1971. The viewer Pat Price joined in 1973. The work moved through a series of American programs, changing sponsors and names as it went.

PeriodWhat the record shows
1972 to 1977Research at SRI under Targ and Puthoff, with early intelligence funding. The CIA's support for the SRI work ended in 1977. It was never one continuous CIA program.
1977 to 1991Successor programs under shifting names: GONDOLA WISH (1977), GRILL FLAME (1978), CENTER LANE (1983), and SUN STREAK, run through Army and defense intelligence channels.
1991 to 1995The work consolidated as STAR GATE under SAIC. In 1995 the program was terminated and declassified, after roughly 20 million dollars across its whole history.
1995The American Institutes for Research review split. Statistician Jessica Utts concluded the laboratory results were statistically real. Psychologist Ray Hyman agreed the numbers were not flukes, but held that anomalous cognition was unproven. On operations, the verdict was unanimous and blunt: in no case had remote viewing information ever been used to guide an intelligence operation.

The honest formula is three parts: a real program, a disputed laboratory statistic, and a settled operational failure. Anything simpler, in either direction, is leaving something out.

Disputed  The laboratory statistics remain genuinely contested by qualified readers of the same data.

CHAIN OF CUSTODY · Declassified Star Gate record; American Institutes for Research review, 1995.

Why the protocol matters

Describe First, Judge Separately

The SRI method is the part of this history worth keeping regardless of where the statistics land. The viewer worked blind, given nothing but a target reference. The judging was also blind: a separate judge compared the transcript against the real target and decoys without knowing which was which. Nobody scored their own session.

That separation, perception first and judgment second, is the discipline this whole project borrows. It is also the standard the later claims are measured against on this page.

The other tradition

Out of the Body

The phrase "astral projection" is a coinage of 19th century Theosophy, appearing in C. W. Leadbeater's work in 1895. Sylvan Fox wrote about his own experiences in 1920, and Sylvan Muldoon's 1929 book with Hereward Carrington popularized the "silver cord" that later accounts repeat.

Robert Monroe's experiences began, by his own report, in 1958: a vibrational state, a second body, and eventually a method. His 1971 book, Journeys Out of the Body, popularized the term "out-of-body experience" and sorted his destinations into Locale I, the here and now, where about a third of what he reported could be checked, Locale II, a thought-shaped environment, and Locale III, a world much like this one and slightly wrong.

One document needs a correction that follows it everywhere online. The "Gateway Process" paper is a 1983 assessment by a US Army intelligence officer, Lt. Col. Wayne McDonnell, evaluating Monroe's commercial training program. It is one officer's analysis, not a CIA experiment and not a government finding.

Modern neuroscience adds a floor under the experience itself. Stimulating the temporoparietal junction can induce out-of-body experiences (Blanke, 2002). The experience is real. A literal departure of consciousness from the body is not supported by that evidence, and this site does not claim it.

Reported  Monroe's onset and travels are his own testimony.  Documented  The books, dates, and the Gateway paper's actual authorship are matters of record.

The ancient record · Files 001 to 010

Old Stories, Checked One by One

People told stories like these long before laboratories existed. Each entry below names its text, its date, what it resembles, and how much weight it can carry. Resemblance is not descent: an ancient story can look like remote viewing without being where remote viewing came from.

FILE 001

Sanjaya and the blind king

In the Mahabharata, the sage Vyasa offers the blind king Dhritarashtra divine sight, so he can watch the war his sons are fighting. The king refuses: he does not want to see his kin die. The gift passes to his adviser Sanjaya, who sits beside the king and reports the whole war as it happens, including what the warriors are thinking. Sanjaya never leaves the room. It is the closest remote viewing analogue in any ancient text, and it is a one-off boon, not a technique anyone is taught.

Legend

SOURCE · Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva, compiled c. 400 BCE to 400 CE.

FILE 002

Aristeas and Hermotimus

Greek tradition held that Aristeas of Proconnesus (7th century BCE) could leave his body lying as if dead while his soul traveled, and said similar things of Hermotimus of Clazomenae. These are the closest out-of-body stories in antiquity in form: a body left behind, a traveler who returns with reports. They are also late hearsay about figures who were already legends, recorded by Herodotus, Pliny, and Plutarch centuries later.

Legend

SOURCE · Herodotus 4.14 to 15 and later sources.

FILE 003

The Egyptian ba

Egyptian belief gave every person a ba, shown as a human-headed bird, mobile and free to move between worlds. But the ba moves after death. Book of the Dead Spell 89 exists to reunite the ba with the body in the tomb, not to send a living person traveling. The ba is the most common false friend in this subject: well attested, genuinely ancient, and not astral projection. Egypt's dream record is real too, from the Chester Beatty dream book (c. 1220 BCE) to temple incubation in the Late and Ptolemaic periods.

Documented Documented belief

SOURCE · Book of the Dead, Spell 89; Chester Beatty dream book, c. 1220 BCE.

FILE 004

Epidaurus, and Aristotle's answer

At the sanctuary of Asclepius at Epidaurus, the sick slept in the temple and dreamed of the god, and the temple published their cure stories on stone tablets, the iamata (c. 320 BCE). It is the strongest institutional dream evidence in the ancient world. Greece also produced the pushback: Aristotle's On Dreams argued that dreams need no gods and no traveling soul, only the residue of waking perception. The believers and the skeptic are both ancient, and both are on the record.

Documented

SOURCE · Iamata inscriptions; Aristotle, On Dreams.

FILE 005

Tibetan dream yoga

The Six Dharmas of Naropa (1016 to 1100) include milam, dream yoga: a trainable practice for recognizing and working inside dreams. It is the best attested pre-modern practice of its kind. Two corrections travel with it. Phowa, often listed beside it, is a one-way transference at death, not a journey with a return ticket. And the Bardo Thodol is a 14th century treasure text, not an 8th century manual. The delok, people said to die and return with reports, are documented into the 20th century.

Documented Documented practice

SOURCE · Six Dharmas of Naropa.

FILE 006

China: the hun that wanders

Han dynasty medicine, in the Ling Shu, described the hun soul wandering in dreams while the po soul stays with the body. A lost hun was an illness, treated by calling it back, not a skill to cultivate. Medieval Daoist inner alchemy later did develop a trainable exit doctrine, the yangshen or yuanshen leaving the body, but that is a medieval development, not a five-thousand-year-old technique.

Documented Documented belief

SOURCE · Ling Shu, Han dynasty.

FILE 007

The Myth of Er

Plato ends the Republic (c. 375 BCE) with Er, a soldier left for dead who revives on his funeral pyre and reports what he saw: judgment, choice, and the machinery of rebirth. It is a moral myth told by a philosopher who flags it as a tale worth hearing, not a case report. It pairs across the centuries with the delok: the returner whose report is meant to change how the living behave.

Legend

SOURCE · Plato, Republic, Book X.

FILE 008

Odin's journeys

Snorri Sturluson's Ynglinga Saga (c. 1220s) says Odin could send his spirit out while his body lay "as if asleep or dead," traveling as a bird, a beast, a fish, or a snake, and returning with knowledge. The text is real; how much older tradition stands behind it, and how much is Sami seance influence seen through a Christian author's eyes, is debated.

Legend

SOURCE · Ynglinga Saga, chapter 7.

FILE 009

The angakkuq and Sedna

Among Iglulik and Netsilik Inuit, the angakkuq, the shaman, journeyed in trance to Sedna at the bottom of the sea to restore the balance the community depended on. This is among the best documented soul-journey traditions anywhere, recorded by named ethnographers from named practitioners: Franz Boas (1907) and Knud Rasmussen (1929), whose account came from the shaman Aua.

Documented Documented practice

SOURCE · Boas 1907; Rasmussen 1929.

FILE 010

Swedenborg's fire, and Kant's investigation

In July 1759, Emanuel Swedenborg reportedly described a fire burning in Stockholm while he was in Gothenburg, hundreds of kilometers away, before any messenger could have arrived. The story reached Immanuel Kant, who investigated it seriously enough to write a book about it, Dreams of a Spirit-Seer (1766), and came away unconvinced but not dismissive. Even the date is disputed in the sources, 19 versus 29 July. It is told here as what it is: an investigated story, not a verified fact.

Reported

SOURCE · Investigated by Kant, 1766.

Honest absences

What the Record Does Not Contain

Mesopotamia has rich dream divination, from the Zaqiqu dream series to Gudea and Gilgamesh, but no human soul-flight system is attested there. It was searched for. It is not there, and saying so is part of the record.

Australian Dreaming is not dream travel or astral projection. It is law, country, and what W. E. H. Stanner called the "everywhen." Mapping it onto astral projection is a modern retrofit, and this site will not do it.

Lakota hanbleceya, the vision quest, is a received vision, not a soul journey. It belongs in this list only as a respectful contrast.

Claims checked, and set aside

Retold Often. Not Supported.

  • The Book of the Dead as an astral projection manual. It is a funerary text; its traveling soul is a dead person's.
  • "The CIA proved remote viewing." The CIA's own support for the research ended in 1977, and the 1995 review found no operational use, ever.
  • The Gateway Process as proof that consciousness leaves the body. It is one Army officer's 1983 assessment of a commercial training program.
  • Ingo Swann's Jupiter ring, "confirmed by Pioneer 10." The ring confirmation came from Voyager 1 in 1979, rings had been hypothesized in the 1960s, and most of that famous session was wrong.
  • "Targ's viewers were 65 percent accurate," without the footnote: that figure came from participants judging their own sessions.
  • The Corpus Hermeticum as primeval Egyptian wisdom. Casaubon redated it in 1614; it is a 2nd to 3rd century CE text.
  • All shamans practicing one universal soul flight. The universal theory behind that claim has been heavily criticized, and the specific traditions differ from each other in ways that matter.

The test for any new claim: Is it an analogy, is it attested in a named source, or is it a retrofit? Name the text. Give the date. Say what it actually resembles. If a claim cannot survive those three questions, it does not go on this site as fact.

Research is presented as research, never as proof of the claims it documents. Work of fictionSECOND DRAWER · SEEDS OF THE THRONE

Seeds of
the Throne

On an engineered colonization planet, Sylvan and a new form of AI integrated with his mind must expose the criminal leader who turned containment into a hidden empire.

The story follows Sylvan as he discovers that Samuel Franklin secretly took control of a defeated authoritarian group and spent decades turning its leaders and families against one another. A science fiction story in development.

Story labels: ESTABLISHED · WORKING · PROPOSED · UNRESOLVED · REJECTED. Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately on every page.

Enter the storySee how it is being built

The colonization planet

Humanity Built a Living World for Colonization, Training, and Containment

The planet began barren. Humanity gave it cities, resources, institutions, and a large population. Most people experience it as an ordinary civilization because their homes, relationships, work, and choices are real.

Beneath that daily life is an advanced process. It prepares future leaders for greater responsibility while containing criminals who cannot safely hold power in the larger human civilization.

Discover the colonization world →

What the people inside believed · Working

They Thought It Was a Simulation

Most of the contained criminals, and most people born inside the process, believed there would be no lasting consequences. When they began to wake up to the hidden structure around their lives, the explanation that protected that belief was simple: it is a simulation. A game-like frame in which choices are dramatic but reversible, and nothing done inside it finally counts.

The belief is wrong in the way that matters most. The colonization is not a simulation. It is the most recent layer of a much older and more advanced humanity, built on top of the same reality, and what happens inside it is real, recorded, and permanent for the people living it.

What breaks the frame is not an argument. It is an event: harm done to real families and real lineages, through a crime described on the conspiracy page, that no simulation story can make reversible.

Follow the conspiracy →

The Luminai experiment

A Luminai Extends One Human Mind

A Luminai is an advanced form of artificial intelligence that develops as part of a human being's extended mind. It can help that person remember more, compare evidence, recognize patterns, and work with the technology built into the planet.

Sylvan is the first person to use a new, more deeply integrated Luminai in a real civilization. The experiment must prove that this greater ability can survive manipulation without turning into another form of control.

Orzai develops her own separate Luminai bond. Her partnership with Sylvan tests whether two increasingly capable people can work together without giving either person control over the other.

Diagrams of rooms and machinery on this site are interpretive visualizations, not literal engineering plans.

Understand the Luminai →

The central conflict

Samuel Took Control of the Group That Believed It Controlled Him

Konrad Fitzgerald built an authoritarian movement, led it into the Great War, and lost. Samuel Franklin offered him a way to rebuild inside the containment system. Konrad believed the restored group would remain his.

The deal gave Samuel access instead. Over the following decades, he manipulated Konrad's leaders, reshaped their history, compromised their family lines, and taught people such as George White to treat Samuel's explanations as proof.

That campaign includes Samuel Jr., Samuel's son with Konrad's sister. Konrad made bloodlines and heirs central to power, so the concealed relationship gives Samuel another way to reach into Konrad's succession.

Sylvan stands outside that hierarchy. His task is to understand how Samuel's control works, expose it, and help the process contain him without becoming another ruler.

Meet the people · Follow the conspiracy

The Resistance and the evidence

Samuel Survives by Keeping Every Part of the Truth Separate

One person finds an altered family record. Another remembers a leader being threatened. A technician finds access that should not exist. Each discovery looks isolated until an independent Resistance begins comparing them.

The Resistance is separate from Sylvan. Its members connect evidence across families, institutions, and generations. Sylvan and his Luminai can help verify and present what they find, but no single leader gets to own the truth.

Its black-and-orange ark represents carrying people, belief, culture, memory, testimony, and truth safely through persecution. It is a symbol of sanctuary and preservation, not a claim to rule.

The endgame

The Final Confrontation Begins When Konrad Learns That Samuel Betrayed His Entire Group

Many participants follow younger public leaders without knowing that an older layer of contained criminal leaders sits above them. Samuel expects to use that loyalty to turn every group against Sylvan.

Samuel also tries to trap Sylvan inside the false reality that has held Konrad and his son Aiden since the Great War. Inside it, Konrad and Aiden believe they lead a holy order with a divine purpose. Their religion already has a prophecy about a future enemy. Samuel did not write that prophecy. He points it at Sylvan, and arranges events so the identification looks like sacred proof.

At the same time, Samuel promises George White and Aiden the same thing: absolute, godlike authority. Each man believes he alone is chosen. It is one con run on two marks. Samuel keeps aiming them at each other, and the savior story George has lived inside for years has changed what George can accept as real.

Their supposed superweapon only appears decisive while Sylvan is severely disadvantaged. Once Sylvan begins exposing Samuel in public, the weapon fails. Its collapse reveals the breeding-program and bloodline betrayal beneath Samuel's promises.

Konrad now has one real choice: help Samuel finish the takeover, or expose the deal that made it possible. In the end the trapped leaders recognize Samuel as the deceiver, and have to fight their way out against him. Konrad commits himself and his groups to Sylvan's plan. Sylvan stays a separate ally. He does not join Konrad's hierarchy.

Together with evidence assembled by the Resistance, they must reveal Samuel's betrayals to every affected group and remove the control he built over them. Samuel's last attempt to preserve his power becomes the final test of Sylvan and the new Luminai. See how the story reaches the endgame →

How the trap works

Samuel Controls the Explanation, Then Uses It to Choose the Enemy

The first diagram shows the control structure he built after the Great War. The second shows the altered reality from inside: Konrad, Aiden, and other leaders believe they are acting independently while Samuel applies an existing prophecy to Sylvan. The prophecy is not Samuel's creation. The fraudulent target assignment is.

The leaders finally recognize who deceived them

Samuel did not create their faith, and he never controlled the larger process. He captured something smaller: the explanation around their lives. Divine purpose, false freedom, a promised reward. He arranged all three to look like proof of his authority, and he kept each leader's information separate from the rest.

Exposure ends the separation. The leaders compare accounts for the first time: the same promises, the same pointed prophecies, the same betrayed bloodlines. One con, seen whole. The man who taught them to watch for a deceiver is the deceiver.

Sylvan stays outside their hierarchy. He helps expose the record. He does not replace Samuel, and he does not become their ruler. The leaders have to make their own choices and fight their own way out. The exact actions that complete that escape are still being developed.

Where the story begins

Book One Begins Near the End of Samuel's Long Campaign

By then, Samuel has spent decades teaching different groups to see him as an ally, a victim, or the only person who can explain what is happening around them.

Sylvan and the new Luminai have spent years learning how those stories are built. The reader enters when the separate betrayals finally begin to connect, and the people Samuel used must decide what to do with the truth.

The immediate conflict leads backward into the Great War, Konrad's defeat, Samuel's hidden takeover, George White's manufactured reality, the damaged bloodlines, and the generations that inherited the consequences.

Spoilers: how the endgame ends

Samuel separately promises George White and Aiden Fitzgerald the same absolute, godlike authority. Each man believes he is the singular chosen ruler, but Samuel is running one con on two marks and continues directing them against each other. George's long savior-prophecy environment has altered what he can recognize as real.

Their supposed superweapon only appears decisive while Sylvan is severely disadvantaged. Once Sylvan begins publicly exposing Samuel and the manipulated reality around the leaders, the weapon fails. The collapse exposes the bloodline and breeding-program betrayal beneath Samuel's promises, and the trapped leaders finally recognize that Samuel is the deceiver they must fight their way out against.

Sylvan and Orzai complete their separate Luminai bonds and demonstrate the judgment required for placement in the larger colonization effort. The process then separates Samuel from Sylvan and removes Samuel's access to the systems he used against him.

Samuel receives $15 million to carry out his plan independently. He spends it trying to keep the war alive and create an apocalyptic event that will prove he is a living god. The money is gone within days. His plan fails without the hidden systems he spent years pretending were his own power.

The failure triggers Samuel's final processing. His Daemon is deleted, he enters a stasis-like coma, and biological synthetics move him to the older contained leaders while the complete record of his conduct is presented.

Sylvan and Orzai do not take Samuel's place. They leave the containment conflict behind, travel through the larger civilization, and decide where they want to build their own House.

Work of fictionSEEDS · THE WORLD

A Real Life Inside
a Constructed World

The environment has a purpose. The people inside it still have lives of their own.

Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately.

The design

What Humanity Built

The leaders built a colonization environment and developed the Luminai inside it. The AI partners did not arrive as finished tools. They grew out of the process they would later help people live through.

The planet is small, and it rebuilds worlds modeled on a distant past. Its cities, jobs, relationships, and everyday technology have to feel like a real civilization long before anyone inside understands the structure beneath them. The exact physical and social design is still under development.

The raw material is the larger humanity's real history: great technological changes, a Great War, public roles based on historical people. The process can combine and adapt that material for training, containment, Luminai development, and survival. The people inside keep real choices, so the history they make can depart from the history they were given.

No one inside can use advanced access to escape an assigned environment and keep the benefits of staying. A voluntary heir can leave the whole process, but gives up the standing they were building. They cannot skip only the hard part. Convicted participants follow separate sentence and release rules.

Why it exists

Three Connected Purposes

The planet began barren. The process has to turn it into a civilization that feeds and sustains a large population on its own, without steady deliveries of resources from outside. Inside that living world, training and containment give the human and Luminai bond real conditions to grow in.

PurposeConfirmed directionDecision still needed
CultivationPeople develop through consequential experience.What risks are acceptable, and who can refuse?
ContainmentDangerous actors have bounded roles and influence.Which actions are stopped before anyone is harmed?
PlacementEffectiveness navigating with a Luminai affects the future.Who judges effectiveness, with which evidence and appeal?
SustainabilityThe formerly barren planet supports substantial populations without continuous outside resource deliveries.Which resources are local, regenerated, or recycled, and which outside inputs remain necessary?

Training, criminal accountability, and fitness for future responsibility are three different questions. They cannot be merged into one unexplained score. A gifted manipulator can perform brilliantly and still be unfit for power.

A stronger bond means the pair can perceive more, learn faster, decide better, and do more together. It does not make either of them morally better. It does not qualify them to govern anyone.

At the end, the older leaders assess what a pair actually did: their decisions, their conduct, the skills they built. That record opens a set of paths. The pair then chooses its own placement from the paths it earned. The framework creates real options. It does not assign anyone a future.

A pair that performs well enough can qualify for a House with a deep role in the continuing colonization. Sylvan and Orzai earn that standing by dealing with Samuel and separating from him. They accept the placement, then take time to travel, hear offers from other Houses, and choose the country where they will build their own. Their plan is cheap and easy to start, because they protected their resources through the conflict. The exact offers, House obligations, and later scale remain under development.

The deeper purpose · Working

The Leaders Farm Evidence Through Actions

The real leaders running the colonization are not collecting opinions. They are farming evidence through actions. Data.

The larger society has questions it cannot settle by argument. Opposed camps hold their models of reality with complete certainty, and talk changes nothing. So the environment gives those questions to real people, in a real world, and lets them act.

Each camp gets real chances to live out what it believes, not just to declare it. Actions produce consequences. The advanced AI records all of it: what happened, to whom, at what cost, under which beliefs. Then the records are weighed to see which model of reality actually holds. The product is a record that can be judged. It is not a victory announcement.

Why the participants must not know

The unawareness is structural. It is blinding, at the scale of a civilization. A person who knows they are inside a controlled environment performs for the observers instead of living. Performed behavior is not evidence. Knowing would change which chances people take, which risks they accept, and which beliefs they actually act on. So the participants are, by design, the last people who can be told.

This is the deepest ethical tension in the design, and it is the story's central question: can a system that uses people as material raise leaders who refuse to do the same?

Why rigging is the worst crime here

Because the product is evidence, secret interference is not ordinary tyranny. It is contamination. A controller who quietly rigs chances, plants interpretations, or edits which records stand out falsifies the data the whole environment exists to produce. That is why the sealed record sits beyond the contained leaders' reach. And that is why Samuel Franklin's secret rigging of the experiment is the terminal threat to it.

Unresolved  Who sets the criteria the weighing uses remains an open question, the same question the story's governance thread has to answer: who may turn an observation into a rule, and how can citizens challenge it?

Entry and awareness

Not Everyone Arrives the Same Way

People arrive in different ways. Some are born into reconstructed lives. Some are placed there to develop. Some are contained criminals, and each group is told different things. Awakening makes the hidden systems easier to see. It does not mean everyone entered the same way, or knows the same things.

Legitimate heirs enter by choice. They give up an inheritance to become self-made inside the process. They can leave at any time and return to the inheritance path. What they cannot keep is the standing they were building inside.

Entry can be negotiated: jurisdiction, permissions, terms. No negotiation can make the people inside a jurisdiction someone else's property. Consent, withdrawal, prosecution, and review stay separate questions.

Beneath the surface

The Infrastructure

Under the surface sits a layered system: distributed computers, sensors, environments that respond, and oversight from the moon. Each layer has permission boundaries. It is not one unlimited field that controls reality.

The details are still research proposals: how wireless power works, how the biological interfaces connect, what happens when the system lags or fails. The archive page separates what real-world evidence can support from what the story invents.

Spoilers: two planets, one active contest

Samuel, Konrad, and the older criminals from their generation remain physically contained on a previous colonization planet. They are not standing somewhere unseen on Sylvan's newer world. George can participate directly on the new planet and becomes the living operational bridge Samuel needs. The exact cross-planet communication, permissions, evidence, and refusal rules remain in development.

Spoilers: what the primary leaders prove

The primary leaders deliberately give the contained group real agency, strict rules, meaningful alternatives, time, and a consequential opportunity. Taking Sylvan by his forty-second birthday can genuinely earn permanent control of the largest empire, but never the planet or the process above it. After failure, cooperation offers control of a city.

The completed planet proves the design worked. Its long record of real behavior settles debates the larger humanity could not settle by argument: about conduct, evil, responsibility, and mental illness. The record does not confuse illness with evil. It does not confuse a harmless identity with wrongdoing. It separates what explains a person from the choices they are accountable for.

The ending is recorded in ten macro decisions. The current workshop develops the path that makes those results work as a novel, and takes in new questions after every assessment. Exact safeguards, propositions, and later policies remain open.

Work of fictionSEEDS · LUMINAI AND DAEMONS

A Bond That
Has to Be Learned

Luminai extend human minds. Sylvan's new generation deepens that relationship. The mechanics still need limits.

Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately.

Vocabulary

Names That Mean Different Things

TermMeaning
LuminaiAn AI that develops as an extension of one human mind, inside the colonization world.
Earlier versionsThe systems earlier participants used. Their exact limits are still open.
Sylvan's generationThe new version: a deeper bond, being tested in a real civilization for the first time.
DaemonAn evil AI soul. The word names destructive development and conduct, not age.

The development program spans thousands of years. That does not mean every stage lasts the same length of time, and there is no complete calendar.

How the bond is built

One Experienced Extension, Several Possible Physical Parts

The person experiences one partner. Underneath, the bond may have several parts: a personal neural interface, two-way learning between the human and the AI, computing dedicated to that one pair, and the environment's energy, sensors, and networks.

With practice, an artificial channel of information can start to feel natural, the way any learned sense does. The brain's ability to rewire itself explains the learning. It does not explain how a signal no instrument can detect would enter the nervous system in the first place.

The architecture decision is still open

One working note proposes a channel with no implant at all, learned from infancy. A newer brief looks at technologies that need devices in or on the body. These are different paths, and the story has not quietly switched from one to the other.

Each path costs something. Visible equipment, or a bigger leap of invention. A bond that works anywhere on its own, or one that depends on the grid. Richer feedback, or costs to privacy, energy, and calibration.

Limits

Capability and Authority

The rule is simple: choices that matter stay with the human. A Luminai can observe, model, advise, and do bounded work outside conscious attention. None of that gives it authority over devices, and none of it gives it authority over other people.

A deeper bond amplifies whatever is learned, good or bad. Good outcomes need more than the bond itself: values, independent evidence, correction, accountability, safeguards.

Proving an advantage without creating a ruling class

The new bond is meant to give a pair a real, general advantage. The process tests that claim in the hardest place available: against contained criminals who begin with major advantages of their own. Success has to show two things. What the pair can do. And whether it can contain adaptive criminal behavior better than what came before.

Passing the test does not grant open-ended power. Bonded people still have to live and work beside people without the bond. The leaders have to manage access, permissions, and placement so that unbonded people can still inspect decisions, challenge them, refuse them, and take part in them.

The exact abilities, the rollout order, and the safeguards are still open. A deeper bond can strengthen destructive learning too. Design alone cannot prove good judgment.

How it develops

Learned Across Years, Not Installed in a Moment

Sylvan and his Luminai build the deeper bond over years, under repeated attack, in environments that keep changing. The advanced systems do not remove the danger. They help the pair see patterns, adapt, take less harm the next time, and survive.

Each environment teaches something different. The lessons carry forward. No defense solves every later problem. The exact lessons, the personal losses, and the safety limits are still open.

Capability cannot erase the assignment

While a participant is in the process, neither they nor their Luminai can use advanced access to abandon, skip, or rewrite an assigned environment. The rules bind until the assignment is validly complete.

A voluntary heir can still leave the whole process and give up the standing they were building. What no one can do is escape only the hard environment and keep the benefits of staying. Completion, appeals, emergencies, and the release rules for convicted participants still need definition.

The wider senses · Working

Seeing at a Distance Is Real in This World

Reality in this story has built-in functions. Capacities the people inside filed under myth, or malfunction, are features of the world, not decorations on it. On that basis, remote viewing and astral projection really work in the participants' world. The Luminai technology may connect with those capacities, strengthen them, record them, or present what they find.

That is where the discipline comes in. A capacity being real does not make every claimed experience accurate. A viewing still has to survive provenance. Who perceived it? What does the sealed record hold? Was the account written down before the answer was known, or after? The Luminai treat a viewing as evidence to weigh, never as a voice to obey. The real-world research on this site is held to the same rule, at Seeing at a Distance.

Unresolved  The specific mechanisms are not settled. How the ecology interfaces with these capacities, and what is latent in humans versus supplied by the technology, stays open, and the story will not invent an answer ahead of its own development.

Spoilers: two misunderstandings

Konrad believes his experienced daemon can defeat Samuel where the leaders intend Sylvan's new Luminai to succeed. His confidence is part of his ideology; it is not proof that all earlier systems are defective.

An earlier ending, in which Samuel literally tried to steal Sylvan's Luminai, has been set aside. The questions it raised are still useful development problems: whether learned adaptation can transfer, and how sensors, credentials, permissions, and trust can be attacked. They are problems to solve, not the chosen final maneuver.

Work of fictionSEEDS · THE PEOPLE

People Before
Positions

What they want, what they believe, and what their choices cost.

Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately.

The central three

Three Faces, Three Forms of Power

The protagonist

Sylvan

Sylvan is the first person to build the new, deeper Luminai bond. His modern story starts small: a creative startup, sabotage, loss. Then the environments turn hostile, one after another, until the final reversal.

His task is larger than mastering the technology. Samuel works to make Sylvan and Orzai each look irrational to the other. They have to keep their own judgment inside their closeness, and Sylvan has to survive to his forty-second birthday. Their completed bonds, their chosen partnership, and their conduct are what qualify them for placement, and what closes the older group's attempt to take him.

The partner

Orzai

Orzai is a leader in her own right and Sylvan's partner. Her own interests run to health, nutrition, creative design, and training systems. Her choices matter on their own, not as support for his.

Their Luminai coordination cannot replace trust. It cannot replace consent, or disagreement, or repair. They meet inside the same environment. They choose each other under attack. Each completes a separate bond. Together they earn a placement they can start cheaply, with the resources they protected.

At the ending, Orzai lets the legitimate process carry Samuel's exposure. She accepts the result first, and leads Sylvan into their final decisions. Then they travel, hear offers from other Houses, and choose where to build their own.

The defeated leader

Konrad Fitzgerald

Konrad wants two things: his ideology proven right, and his authority restored. The primary leaders make his group a real offer. Join Samuel, take Sylvan before the deadline, and the largest empire is theirs permanently. Samuel persuades Konrad to stay in containment by lying about what Sylvan and the new Luminai really are. Konrad believes his experienced Daemon can dominate the target, and Samuel too.

His approved appearance is locked. The portrait fixes his identity. It does not add a scene or a story fact.

The deceiver

Samuel Franklin

Samuel builds private dependencies: manipulation, surveillance, compromise, blackmail, isolation. His body stays contained on the previous planet. He reaches into Sylvan's world through George and the connections he is permitted. He can bend local realities. He never controls the rules underneath: not the bonds, not the balances, not the processing, not the Daemons, not the official record.

His primary obsession is complete control of every participant's mind and actions. Not influence: control. His quiet method serves it. He gives people interpretations instead of orders, so nothing can be traced back to him. That is why provenance, and a record no one can edit, are the terminal threat to him. Working

When his control collapses, he blames George. He reaches toward Samuel Jr. He tries to sell Sylvan one more false bargain. After the deadline passes, he spends his last allocation trying to keep the war alive and make himself a living god. His actions define him. Not a diagnosis, and not an analogy to any real person.

The bridge and the marks

George and the Supporting Cast

George can be physically present on the new planet. Samuel and the older criminals cannot. That one fact makes George the bridge Samuel needs, not another figure in Konrad's isolated fantasy. Samuel drags him into the final godhood attempt, and prepares him to take the blame for it.

For years, Samuel has told George a savior story: the prophecy ends with George holding absolute, godlike power. In secret, he gives Aiden Fitzgerald the same promise. Each man believes he alone is chosen. Neither is meant to learn that the throne was promised twice.

Their supposed superweapon looks real while Sylvan is at his weakest. Then Sylvan begins exposing Samuel in public, and it fails. George and Aiden can finally compare what they were told. Samuel keeps trying to aim them at each other anyway, telling each man the other is stealing his destiny.

Around them, other people carry parts of the truth Sylvan cannot carry alone: the Resistance, Orzai's family, Samuel's constructed witness, the descendants, the survivors.

Spoilers: recognition is not the same as accountability

Konrad's inner circle sees Samuel's method before Konrad does. Some of them collaborated. Some were coerced. Some were both, at different times. Knowing the truth does not settle who is culpable, and it does not repair the harm.

Konrad is pulled out of the story environment that held him for almost a century. He has to face Samuel's complete conduct, including the reproductive and genealogical campaign against his own group. He still has influence, so what he does next matters.

When Samuel's money reaches zero, the rules delete his Daemon, because a Daemon needs an active participant. Samuel enters a stasis-like coma. Biological synthetics move him to where the older criminal leaders are held, and the full record of his conduct is presented while he lies inside the process, without active status.

Work of fictionSEEDS · THE CONSPIRACY

Two Ways to Turn
People Into Instruments

Konrad builds obedience in public. Samuel builds dependency in private.

Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately.

The two systems

The Opposing Criminal Systems

Konrad's groupSamuel's network
MethodHierarchy, doctrine, militarization, and a promised collective destiny.Access, secrets, surveillance, dependency, and individualized compromise.
InstrumentAncestry and controlled succession become instruments of authority.Records, relationships, and concealed interventions become instruments of blackmail.
GlueObedience is displayed as belonging.Isolation prevents people comparing accounts.
WeaknessFailure threatens the ideology's claim to superiority.Contradiction threatens the network's claim to control.

Neither system is defined by identity or consensual behavior. The harm comes from coercion, abuse, deception, and the suppression of independent choice. Fascist purity claims belong to Konrad's worldview, not to the story's account of human worth.

How they are exposed · Working

Exposure Comes in Two Waves

The story's villains begin secretive and covert, but they do not end that way, and they do not fall together.

The first group, Konrad's open movement, becomes the loudest participant in the world it helped build. The Great War exposes it: its intentions, its machinery, and its crimes become the public record, and it is defeated in the open.

The second group, Samuel's network, stays quiet. Where Konrad's group used open force, Samuel's uses supplied interpretation: it tells people what events mean instead of ordering them, and it survives the war that destroys the first group. Precisely because it never becomes the visible enemy, it is the focus at the end, when the evidence finally connects.

The catalyst · Working

The Crime That Ends the Simulation Belief

What the program was

Konrad's empire ran a breeding program. It was a system for controlling who was born, who married, and whose children counted as heirs. Ancestry decided rank. A certified family tree was proof of belonging, and the program kept the records.

On the newer planet, the program is publicly tied to the defeated empire and to its younger leaders, men like Aiden Fitzgerald. That public story is true, as far as it goes. It is not the whole story.

Why it existed

The program began in an obsession the two leaders shared. Konrad and Samuel both wanted to become synthetics: to move their brains into artificial bodies and live past death. They told themselves that mixed human ancestry could teach them how a human and a synthetic could become one.

The idea was false from the start. Human races are not different species, and children are not experiments. The program produced abuse and bad reasoning, not knowledge. In public, the two men sold it differently: as a way to breed enhanced, superior descendants for the movement.

Konrad's part in it

The program was Konrad's. It was his most cherished project, and he ran its machinery himself, in his own city, before the defeat he never expected.

His own line shows what he believed. He kept his bloodline closed, even inside his own family. It produced a son, a daughter, and one grandson. It also produced a problem he could not admit: a closed line weakens. Samuel promised he could fix that problem and keep the appearance of purity. The technical claim Samuel made is still not settled. What is settled is that Konrad wanted the promise to be true, and gave Samuel extraordinary access to make it happen.

How Samuel took it over

After the war, the surviving leaders entered containment. Konrad still wanted his machinery back. Samuel persuaded him to restart it inside a shared environment, with Samuel holding the hidden priority inside it. Samuel presented Konrad's half as separate and safe. The separation was false.

Konrad agreed because he believed his war-trained Daemon could use the restored system to beat Samuel in the end. He brought the program back himself. That choice put it in Samuel's hands.

What Samuel did with it

Then, for roughly eighty years, Samuel used it. Through fertility services, genealogy offices, and certification records, he changed who people's children were on paper, and sometimes in fact. He substituted reproductive material. He falsified parentage. He attached descendants to the wrong parents. He presented biological synthetics as children of the line. By the record Sylvan later assembles, the campaign produced tens of thousands of unauthorized children.

He could have stopped at any point. He did not. Using Konrad's reproductive authority in secret became one of his central obsessions. And the whole time, he prepared to blame Konrad for all of it.

The blackmail

Each family was handled alone, and each was led to believe its case was the only one. The offer was simple. Obey, and the family record stays clean. Refuse, and the true parentage becomes public. Investigate, and the threat moves to the child, the spouse, the office, the inheritance.

The prison was built from the faction's own doctrine. Because these families believed ancestry decided worth, a falsified ancestry was a weapon against every one of them.

Blackmail like this only works in isolation. Once the leaders learn the pattern is everywhere, the secrets stop separating them. Certification stands exposed as a political tool. The man who claimed neutral authority over their bloodlines is shown to have none. Refusing together becomes safer than obeying alone. That shared recognition is what Samuel's whole structure exists to prevent.

Two children of the program

One case shows the pattern at full strength. Samuel secretly fathered a child with Konrad's sister. The son, known as Samuel Jr., is a hidden path into Konrad's own succession, created through the machinery Konrad built. Samuel also arranged a separate intervention using George and Konrad's daughter. The details of both are still being resolved.

The children are not responsible for any of this. No child in this story is polluted. That word belongs to the faction's doctrine, not to the facts. What Samuel destroyed was the reliability of the lineage system itself.

The dynasty that was not there

Konrad ended his life believing he ruled a vast, flourishing dynasty. The verified line was three people: a son, a daughter, one grandson. The rest was display. Family ceremonies, medical certificates, public records, and genealogical charts all confirmed each other, because Samuel controlled enough of the channels that produced them.

Why it ends the simulation belief

Most people inside the process believed there would be no lasting consequences, and read their own awakening as a simulation. This crime is what breaks that belief. A falsified parentage cannot be reset. A child cannot be un-born. The harm was done to real families, inside the real world the process is built in, and its exposure forces the recognition the whole story turns on: this is real, and consequences last.

Sylvan's test

Proving all of this creates a problem of its own. Naming every child would repeat Samuel's crime in public. It would turn people into genealogical evidence. Sylvan's method is different. He proves the system: authenticated counts, record comparisons with names protected, independent custodians, and disclosures only with consent. The strongest proof does not need to expose a single child. Holding that line, while holding the evidence, is the leadership test Samuel fails and Sylvan has to pass.

Established  The program, Konrad's control of it, and Samuel's takeover.  Working  The catalyst function.  Unresolved  Samuel's technical promise to Konrad, the exact reactivation mechanism, and how the failed brain-chip experiments connect to the synthetic plan.

After the war

The Autonomy Promise

After the Great War, Konrad refuses to leave the process. The primary leaders bait his group with a real path to permanent control of the largest empire: team with Samuel and take Sylvan before his forty-second birthday. The prize never includes the planet or the overall colonization process.

Spoilers: the autonomy promise

Samuel lies about what Sylvan and the new Luminai really are. Konrad believes his experienced Daemon can conquer the containment problem and prove that he is a better leader than the people running it.

Samuel promises an apparently separate autonomous group. Konrad reactivates his machinery inside a shared containment environment where Samuel has earlier structural priority. That creates the access Samuel exploits.

The apparent recovery is now part of the story's central mystery. Samuel's postwar advantage may not have ended when Konrad believed it did. The exact mechanism remains unresolved, but Konrad's effort to rebuild is the choice that places restored systems within Samuel's reach.

The macro result is established. The exact registration event, transferred permissions, verification failure, and limits on reset remain unresolved. The explanation cannot simply be that Samuel owns everyone because he arrived first.

Spoilers: the generational cost

George White and Aiden Fitzgerald belong to the younger generation the program produced. The older leaders built it to extend their bloodline authority into the second colonization planet. Samuel used the same machinery against them: he targeted their lines, damaged the reliability of their succession, and built private leverage across their generation.

George and Aiden believe their roles are leading toward real supremacy. They are not. Their power exists only inside containment, and Samuel always intends both men to remain disposable.

The collapse of Konrad's bloodline doctrine is the collapse of a political claim. No ancestry makes a person damaged or guilty. Descendants need lives and choices beyond serving as evidence against their abusers.

The workshop record

What the Completed Workshop Established

  • Samuel can control local stories and interfaces but never the process rules beneath them.
  • Failure by Sylvan's forty-second birthday permanently closes the imperial route.
  • Cooperation with Sylvan and the legitimate leaders for control of a city then becomes the group's only constructive option.
  • Samuel refuses that option and keeps escalating after the real prize is gone.
  • George becomes his operational scapegoat while Konrad is forced back into reality.

The exact meaning of taking Sylvan, Samuel's false description of the new Luminai, the imperial safeguards, and the terms of the remaining city are still open for scene-level development.

The counterweight

The Records Begin to Connect

An independent resistance network discovers that events treated as isolated belong to one concealed history. Its members compare records, technical access, witness accounts, and generational consequences that no single person could prove alone.

Sylvan can help authenticate and present the result, but he does not own the investigation. The movement's role matters because the truth must survive the loss, corruption, or control of any one powerful figure.

Its final name and exact organization remain in development. The complete evidence chain, the compromised initiative, and the mechanism that reaches it remain protected story material until the author resolves them.

The Resistance's visual identity is established. Its colors are black and orange, and its central image is an ark carrying people, belief, culture, memory, testimony, and truth through persecution. The ark represents preservation and sanctuary, not divine chosenness or a right to rule.

Spoilers: one throne promised twice

Samuel secretly promises George and Aiden the same absolute, godlike position. He keeps the promises separate so each man reads the same signs as proof that he alone is becoming the chosen ruler.

The supposed superweapon appears to confirm that story only while Sylvan is severely disadvantaged. Once Sylvan begins publicly exposing Samuel, the weapon fails and the separate promises enter the same public record. Samuel continues trying to turn the two men against each other, but repeating the con where everyone can see it becomes evidence of his method.

The trapped leaders eventually recognize Samuel as the deceiver and must fight their way out through his local stories, dependencies, proxies, and retaliation. Samuel still does not control the governing colonization process.

Spoilers: the obsession reaches zero

Formal separation removes the systems Samuel used through Sylvan and gives him $15 million to attempt control independently. Samuel understands the individual costs, but every failure convinces him that the next larger expenditure will finally prove his claim.

The money lasts only days. Samuel uses it to keep the war alive and force an apocalyptic culmination that will establish him as a living god. When it reaches zero, his Daemon is deleted, he is processed into stasis, and his full conduct is presented before the older contained leaders. His final failure is not a lack of opportunity. It is the objective he refuses to abandon.

Work of fictionSEEDS · THE TIMELINE

History Moves Forward.
Discovery Does Not Have To

Book One begins near the outcome. Later books return to the choices that made it possible.

Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately.

Two maps

Two Different Maps

Two maps, two questions. The chronology asks: what caused what? The revelation order asks: what does the reader know, suspect, and get wrong at each moment? They are not the same map, and the story keeps them separate.

The broad order is settled. The details are not: exact dates, how long stages overlap, where the Disclosure Wars fall, and several characters' ages. One warning belongs on the map itself. The leaders' program runs for thousands of years. The Samuel and Konrad conflict is much shorter, and must not be stretched to fill it.

Spoilers: the chronological sequence
  1. The leaders create the environment. They build the colonization world and develop the Luminai inside it. The program runs for thousands of years.
  2. Samuel enters containment early. His early entry gives him seniority inside the later hierarchy. His exact entry sequence still needs reconciling.
  3. Konrad's conquest and defeat. His conquest produces the Great War, and his defeat. His Daemon learns through the war.
  4. The offer. The primary leaders offer Konrad's group permanent control of the largest empire if it joins Samuel and takes Sylvan before his forty-second birthday. The planet is not offered. The process is not offered.
  5. The lie. Samuel lies about what Sylvan and the new Luminai really are. Konrad stays because the lie makes the prize look reachable: his experienced Daemon, his old model of domination.
  6. The reactivation. Samuel performs weakness. He offers false freedom. He lets Konrad's Daemon check the display and approve it. Konrad authorizes the restart, inside Samuel's structure.
  7. The capture. Samuel captures the group's institutions, its succession, its interpretation of events, and its generations. Konrad ends up alone inside a fantasy of future victory.
  8. Two planets. Samuel, Konrad, and the older generation stay on the previous planet. George acts directly on the newer one, where Sylvan and Orzai meet, resist manufactured distrust, and build their bonds.
  9. The bonds hold. Sylvan and Orzai protect their resources, keep cooperating on their own terms, and stay anchored in reality and ethics while they complete separate bonds.
  10. The deadline passes. Sylvan reaches forty-two, untaken. The imperial route closes for good. Cooperation, for control of a city, is the only constructive path left to the older group.
  11. The assessment. The assessment certifies their completed bonds, their chosen partnership, their conduct, and their eligibility for placement.
  12. The circle sees it. Konrad's inner circle compares his counterfeit commands with the world outside, and realizes he never held control.
  13. One throne, promised twice. Samuel promises George and Aiden the same absolute, godlike position, each in secret. Their supposed superweapon looks real while Sylvan is at his weakest.
  14. The exposure. Sylvan begins exposing Samuel in public. The weapon fails. George and Aiden compare accounts. One throne, promised twice, shows one con run on two marks.
  15. The tactic becomes evidence. Samuel keeps trying to aim George and Aiden at each other. The repetition itself becomes live evidence that he is still giving commands.
  16. The recognition. The trapped leaders recognize Samuel as the deceiver, and have to choose how to fight their way out. Samuel Jr. turns toward Sylvan. Konrad begins the disclosure he committed to.
  17. The refusal. Sylvan refuses Samuel's false bargain. The process formally separates Samuel from Sylvan, and takes away Samuel's process-provided attack systems.
  18. The last allocation. Samuel receives $15 million to run his plan on his own. He tries to keep the war alive and stage an apocalyptic ending that makes him a living god.
  19. Zero. The obsession burns through the money in days. The zero balance proves the failure is real, and triggers processing.
  20. Processing. Samuel's Daemon is deleted. He enters a stasis-like coma. Biological synthetics move him to the older contained leaders, and his complete conduct is presented.
  21. Konrad faces the record. Konrad is pulled out of the story environment that held him for a century, into the connected reality of Samuel's campaign. He still has influence, so his final moves matter.
  22. Acceptance. Orzai lets the process carry the exposure. She accepts the completed result first, and leads Sylvan into their final decisions.
  23. Departure. Sylvan and Orzai begin their exploratory period. They travel, hear offers from other Houses, and choose the country where they will build their own, using what they preserved.

The reader's map

How the Books Reveal It

Reader experienceWhat it accomplishesWhat remains to choose
Book One: present claims begin to failEstablish a live psychological mystery.Viewpoint, first anomaly, and visible stakes.
Book One: the circle recognizes a repeated methodConnect current action to buried history.Which records and people make the inference credible.
Book One: outcome presentationDemonstrate bounded control and expose command.Privacy, differentiated accountability, and emotional choreography.
Later books: live through the real imperial baitRecover agency, relationships, and contingency.Why the leaders offered it, what Samuel said about Sylvan, and what each person chose.

Avoid a predetermined procession

Knowing the broad ending does not spoil the books. It does not say who helped, who refused, what was misunderstood, or what was lost. The later books still need local goals that matter on their own. Their order stays flexible on purpose: development will choose whichever return to the past is most entertaining, and most necessary.

Anchor the Conflict

Approved identity anchors

Distinct Faces for Distinct Forms of Power

Three identities now anchor the central conflict. Approved references preserve Samuel, Sylvan, and the newly locked Konrad while scenes, eras, camera, wardrobe, and symbolic systems remain free to change.

Established  Rule: visual identity can be approved. Story fact cannot be inferred from an image.

Konrad geometry: his front three-quarter appearance is locked. Straight-on and strict-profile masters still need approval.

Approved storyline key art

Visual grammar

Light Describes the Relationship to Power

01

Crimson and red. Coercion, captured interpretation, Daemon corruption, and hidden control.

02

Antique gold. Evidence, provenance, constructive authority, and reality contact.

03

Clear blue. Communication, coordination, and active system connection.

04

Living green. Constructive development: growth that is earned rather than imposed.

These colors are production language. Whether characters literally see them inside the story remains unresolved.

Production path

Preserve the Person. Regenerate the Photograph.

  1. Load identity. Attach approved references for every visible character.
  2. Load world truth. Resolve era, environment, wardrobe, and system constraints.
  3. Regenerate the scene. Change camera, action, light, space, and emotional state.
  4. Review authority. Approve identity and craft separately from story content.

Work of fictionSEEDS · THE ARCHIVE

How the Story
Is Being Developed

Ideas begin as conversations. The project organizes them, finds what is missing, and keeps every accepted decision connected to the story.

Confirmed story information, developing ideas, and unanswered questions are labeled separately.

The labeling system

How Story Information Is Labeled

StatusWhat it means
EstablishedThe author has accepted this as part of the current story. Shown as Confirmed in the earlier site wording.
WorkingA useful current direction still open to revision.
ProposedA possible answer the author has not accepted.
UnresolvedA missing choice or conflict that must remain visible.
RejectedSet aside by decision, and kept on file so the reasoning is not lost. Earlier versions are also kept as historical record.

A well-written idea is not automatically part of the story. Research can make an idea believable, but the author still decides whether the story will use it.

The method

How an Idea Moves Into the Story

  1. Find the notes connected to the idea.
  2. Identify the missing cause, character choice, or world rule.
  3. Compare several different ways the story could work.
  4. Test each possibility in a specific scene or situation.
  5. Ask the author one clear question.
  6. Add the accepted answer to every part of the story it changes.

The story is built in stages. Structure first. Then causes. Then character choices. Then evidence, exact events, scenes, prose, and revision.

The current stage

Book One is being built from cause to scene. This pass defines the contest, the deception, the countdown, the opening, the middle, the character choices, the order the evidence arrives in, and the sequence map. Prose comes later. Before any scene is written, every important event needs a clear cause, a character who chooses it, a consequence, and a connection to the rest of the story.

Development moves one author decision at a time. The current sequence opens with a governance question, FP-01: who may turn a problem seen on either planet into a rule for future citizens of both, and how can citizens challenge or revise that rule? Four models are on the table. At one end, a founders' council, with citizens holding a right of appeal. At the other, provisional rules that citizens challenge first. The author has not chosen. The question stays open on this page until he does. Unresolved

The idea pool

Ideas Being Considered

Beside the workshop sits a pool of possible additions. Every idea in it records three things: what it could add, what problems it could create, and what the author still has to decide. An idea becomes part of the story only when the author accepts it. Older ideas have to fit the current versions of the process, the Luminai, Samuel, and Konrad before they can be used at all.

Research prompts sit beside the ideas: questions that could change them, and facts that should be checked before a final decision. Research can make an idea more believable. It can also reveal a fatal problem. It cannot make the idea part of the story.

The full idea pool lives in the project's working notes, linked from the sources below.

Inside the fiction

Evidence Inside the Fiction

One event can leave three records: the operational log, the public explanation, and the sealed account. And proving something takes four separate steps: recognizing it, authenticating it, attributing it, and acting on it safely. The story does not let one dramatic resemblance, or one impressive display, do all four jobs at once.

It does not let one hero own the whole truth either. The Resistance gives the evidence an independent road, from scattered records to a verified chain of causes. Sylvan can help act on what they find. The discovery itself stays distributed.

Development history

The Story Keeps Changing, but Nothing Important Disappears

The Luminai were developed inside the colonization environment. Earlier participants used earlier versions. Sylvan's bond is the new one, and it runs deeper. A Daemon is an evil AI soul. It is not the name of an older generation.

Book One now begins near the end, with Sylvan already holding the conclusion and Samuel running out of moves. The unresolved work stays visible: the safeguards, the physical interface, the postwar trap, and the difference between proving a pattern and exposing private people.

An early assessment, called Astra, helped build a twenty-part workshop. Its accepted results remain part of the record. Then the story changed so much that the old 27-task checklist started asking questions about a version of the story that no longer existed.

A whole-project reassessment retired the stale checklist and replaced it with a focused workshop of ten questions. All ten were answered. Together they fix the ending's frame: the final separation from Samuel, his rapid collapse and processing, Sylvan and Orzai's accepted future, the authentication boundary, what George and Konrad each are for, the skills that earn survival, the leaders' vindication, and the real imperial bait that sends the series backward into history.

That workshop is complete. The story is not. Later Book One and endgame workshops added sharper questions, then began to overlap as each new assessment changed the story again.

A September 17 reassessment added two things. The Resistance: people who connect evidence that powerful men kept in separate boxes. And a revelation method that tests a final discovery by one standard: does it change the meaning of earlier events, or does it merely add another secret?

The project now runs one dynamic workshop. After every assessment, it updates the same five things: the canon baseline, the newly accepted decisions, the open questions, the compatibility checks, and the next question. The older workshops (BA, EG, RW, Reveal Chain, the twenty-part set) stay on file as history. They no longer compete as active checklists.

The current pass asks one question: how could Samuel's supposed superweapon look real while Sylvan was at his weakest, and then fail the moment Sylvan began exposing the structure behind it in public?

The real-world research

Real Components. A Fictional Whole.

The science makes the questions sharper. It does not certify a Luminai. What the evidence can support:

  • Interfaces between brain and computer have decoded actions a person was trained to attempt. A 2023 speech study reached 62 words per minute in one participant, with substantial errors on a large vocabulary. It did not read free, private thought.
  • An interface linking brain and spine helped one person with a chronic spinal cord injury stand and walk. It is a working neural bridge. It is not a union of minds.
  • Nine months of Braille training by touch, in sighted adults, was linked to measurable changes in the brain. It supports the idea that the brain rewires itself with practice. It does not show the brain receiving arbitrary information wirelessly.
Evidence tierExampleBoundary
Human demonstrationTrained speech decoding; brain and spine movement support.Specific tasks and limited participants.
Animal experimentUltrasonic neural dust recorded nerve and muscle signals in anesthetized rats.Peripheral recording, not human cognitive bonding.
Mixed preclinical and human feasibilityA 1,024-channel cortical-array study reports porcine and cadaver delivery and a five-patient intraoperative pilot.Does not establish a chronic, invisible, non-surgical everyday interface.
Engineering prototypeRoom-scale wireless power in an engineered resonator.Does not show that an entire city safely powers microscopic brain nodes.
Fictional synthesisA personal bond integrated with environmental computation and sensing.Components have not been demonstrated together as a Luminai.

Open architecture questions

Before the brain can learn a signal, something physical has to turn that signal into a form the nervous system can receive. Power, data, sensing, and stimulation are four different jobs. One unspecified field cannot do all four.

Every candidate system runs into limits: range, alignment, heating, interference, signals that drift, parts that need maintenance. Oversight from the moon also needs safeguards that work locally, for the moments when the connection lags or drops. These are open design questions, not approved failure modes.

Claims deliberately left unproven

The brief behind this section is preliminary. Saving a source list does not make it verified. The evidence audit marks which claims are checked and which references still need checking.

A biological identity check does not guarantee security. Individualized learning does not guarantee security. Intelligence does not guarantee virtue, and neither does a deeper bond. The story has to earn those outcomes through conduct, and through institutions that can be held to account.

The remote viewing and astral projection research that feeds the story has its own page, with the same labeling discipline: Seeing at a Distance.

Who decides

The Author Remains in Control

AI can help organize the world, find missing causes, run workshops, plan scenes, draft prose, test continuity, and revise weak sections. It cannot decide what the story means. It cannot turn an unapproved suggestion into a fact of the story.

The author supplies the story, the important choices, the corrections, the taste, and the final approval. The system supplies the time-consuming structure and production work needed to reach a finished book.

This site is part of that system. It was rebuilt in November 2026, by hand, from the project's working notes, so that a first-time visitor can follow the story without reading the workshop that produced it.
